newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds fall after Brazil court ruling.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds fall after Brazil court ruling.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Wednesday after a Brazilian court voted in favor of a 28.9 percent pay rise to 11 civil servants.
Traders were spooked by the ruling which could serve as a precedent for the entire Brazilian federal workforce, costing the government billions.
"There was bad news out of Brazil which frightened people a bit," said a trader at a local bank.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell 3/8 to 91, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was $0.10 lower at 126.35.
The market was already lethargic before the ruling in the afternoon, suffering from a lack of market flows and soft U.S. Treasuries.
"The market is heavy," said another trader.
This week's slow action has some traders suggesting a correction, which they see as overdue, may be about to hit the market. The dire shortage of market volume has added to that sentiment.
Still, on the positive side Wednesday, the FIEL consultancy said January industrial production rose 11.4 percent from the same month a year earlier.
Call money rates fell to 6.48 percent from 6.53 percent.
